subject: Occurrence distribution rasters are inverted from R?

messages.author: 73db0f7e944f4290
messages.subject: Occurrence distribution rasters are inverted from R?
parts:
Hi Chris,

I exported my kriged occurrence distributions as rasters and noticed that the values are inverted from those plotted in R. From the R plot immediately below, I read that this animal had a high probability of occurring in the the darker blue spots at any random time within my observation period. However, when I viewed the TIF raster I exported from R in ArcMap 10.3 (screenshot), the values are reversed with darker blue spots from the R plot being colored as white low probability spots. Am I interpreting these figures correctly?



> plot(wht11_krige, DF = "CDF")


> writeRaster(x = wht11_krige, DF = "CDF", filename = "OD_rasters/wht11_krige_CDF", format = "GTiff")



Thank you in advance!
-Emily

messages.author: ec946d16b0c85849
messages.subject: Re: Occurrence distribution rasters are inverted from R?
parts:
It's very common for TIFF files have the color reversed because the mishandling of various software. It could be either in R side or ArcMap side.

https://support.esri.com/en/technical-article/000001302

https://www.google.com/search?q=tiff+color+reversed

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Occurrence distribution rasters are inverted from R?
parts:
Hi Emily,

That looks correct for the CDF. The CDF ranges from 0 at the innermost contour to 1 at the outermost contour. High CDF value does not mean high probability but high quantile value. E.g., the 95% contour is defined by CDF=0.95.

If you had exported the PDF or PMF, then it would have been as you expected.

Best,
Chris
